title: UVM data sources: shared connector facts, availability, and the Jira, Zscaler, Okta, Code42, NetBox, runZero, SecurityScorecard and SFTP connectors

prose.text: The shared Configure > Sources procedure is in [[portfolio.secops-platform:data-sources]]; the connector pages add the facts below. AnySource is in [[uvm.anysource]] and the other connectors are in [[uvm.data-sources.cloud]], [[uvm.data-sources.endpoint]], [[uvm.data-sources.appsec]] and [[uvm.data-sources.inventory]]. Product overview: [[uvm.overview]].

checks.do: Whether the connector page marks the connector, or a stream, as limited availability before relying on it.
Whether the credential for the source was saved when generated: the pages for these connectors say it cannot be copied or viewed later.

limited-availability.statement: Among the connector pages, these state that the connector is in limited availability and to contact Zscaler Support: Aqua Security, Burp Suite Issues, Claroty xDome for Healthcare, CyCognito, Datto, Dragos, Endor Labs, GitHub Advanced Security, GitHub Repositories, Google Cloud Platform, Halo Assets, HCL BigFix - Computers, Ionix and Mandiant ASM; the Horizon3.ai page says this of its Weaknesses Evidence stream.

quotes: The Aqua Security connector is in limited availability. To learn more, contact Zscaler Support.
The Burp Suite Issues connector is in limited availability. To learn more, contact Zscaler Support.
The Claroty xDome for Healthcare connector is in limited availability. To learn more, contact Zscaler Support.
The CyCognito connector is in limited availability. To learn more, contact Zscaler Support.
The Datto connector is in limited availability. To learn more, contact Zscaler Support.
The Dragos connector is in limited availability. To learn more, contact Zscaler Support.
The Endor Labs connector is in limited availability. To learn more, contact Zscaler Support.
The GitHub Advanced Security connector is in limited availability. To learn more, contact Zscaler Support.
The GitHub Repositories connector is in limited availability. To learn more, contact Zscaler Support.
The GCP connector is in limited availability. To learn more, contact Zscaler Support.
The Halo Assets connector is in limited availability. To learn more, contact Zscaler Support.
The HCL BigFix - Computers connector is in limited availability. To learn more, contact Zscaler Support.
The Horizon3 Weaknesses Evidence stream is in limited availability. To learn more, contact Zscaler Support.
The Ionix connector is in limited availability. To learn more, contact Zscaler Support.
The Mandiant ASM connector is in limited availability. To learn more, contact Zscaler Support.

auth-immutable.statement: For the Okta Workforce Identity and CrowdStrike Falcon Insights sources, once the data source is saved its authentication cannot be changed; to use a different authentication, delete the data source and create a new one.

quotes: After the data source is saved, you can't change its authentication. To use a different authentication, delete the existing data source and create a new one.
After the data source is saved, you can't change its authentication. To use a different authentication, delete the existing data source and create a new one.

credential-shown-once.statement: On the pages for these connectors, the credential generated in the third-party product cannot be copied or viewed later (Apiiro token, Axonius API key and secret, Bitsight token, Black Duck token, Burp Suite API key, Claroty token, Code42 secret, CyCognito API key, Datto secret, Flexera refresh token, Horizon3.ai API key, Ionix token, Legit Security token); the Halo Assets page adds that saving the application before copying means the client secret must be regenerated while the client ID is unchanged.

quotes: Save the token securely as you cannot copy or view it later.
Save the API key and API secret securely as you cannot copy or view it later.
Save the token securely as you cannot copy or view it later.
Save the token securely as you cannot copy or view it later.
Save the API key securely as you cannot copy or view it later.
Save the token securely as you cannot copy or view it later.
Save the secret securely as you cannot copy or view it later.
Save the API key securely as you cannot copy or view it later.
Save the secret securely as you cannot copy or view it later.
Save the refresh token securely as you cannot copy or view it later.
Save the API key securely as you cannot copy or view it later.
Save the token securely as you cannot copy or view it later.
Save the token securely as you cannot copy or view it later.
If you save the application before copying the client ID and client secret, you must regenerate the client secret and copy it. The client ID remains unchanged.

token-inherits-user.statement: Several connector pages say the generated token or key carries the permissions of the creating user: Bitsight and Ionix tokens, and the AttackForge API key.

quotes: The generated token inherits the access permissions associated with the user creating it.
The generated token inherits the access permissions associated with the user creating it.
The API key inherits the access permissions of the user who created it and is restricted to the data they are allowed to access within the AttackForge platform.

stream-selection.statement: Connector pages with several streams say to select the streams that match your feature plan and use cases; the Apiiro, Aqua Security, Armis, AWS, Bitsight, CrowdStrike, Cyera, Datto, Dragos and Endor Labs pages state this.

quotes: There are three Apiiro streams. Select those that are based on your Apiiro feature plan and use cases:
There are 7 Aqua Security streams. Select those that are based on your Aqua Security feature plan and use cases:
There are three Armis streams. Select those that are based on your Armis feature plan and use cases:
There are 10 AWS streams. Select those that are based on your AWS feature plan and use cases:
There are two Bitsight streams. Select those that are based on your Bitsight feature plan and use cases:
There are 5 CrowdStrike streams. Select those that are based on your CrowdStrike feature plan and use cases:
There are two Cyera streams. Select those that are based on your Cyera feature plan and use cases:
There are two Datto streams. Select those that are based on your Datto feature plan and use cases:
There are two Dragos streams. Select those that are based on your Dragos feature plan and use cases:
There are 5 Endor Labs streams. Select those that are based on your Endor Labs feature plan and use cases:

days-to-fetch-defaults.statement: Lookback behavior differs by page: by default the Aqua Security connector retrieves data from the last 7 days, the Digital Shadows connector from the last 30 days, and the Axonius connector retrieves all data; on the Bitsight page, if the field is left empty, all available data is retrieved.

quotes: By default, the connector retrieves data from the last 7 days.
By default, the connector retrieves data from the last 30 days.
By default, the connector retrieves all data.
If left empty, all available data is retrieved.

large-range-timeouts.statement: The Aqua Security and Digital Shadows pages warn that a larger date range can lead to longer processing times or potential timeouts.

quotes: Selecting a larger date range might lead to longer processing times or potential timeouts.
Selecting a larger date range can lead to longer processing times or potential timeouts.

jira-issues-stream.statement: The Jira Issues stream retrieves standard issue and custom fields; its project setting is a comma-separated list of Jira project keys and, if left empty, issues from all projects accessible to the user are fetched.

quotes: The Jira Issues stream retrieves standard issue and custom fields.
A comma-separated list of Jira project keys to replicate data from. If left empty, the connector fetches issues from all projects accessible to the user.

jira-auth-fields.statement: The Jira Issues authentication takes an API Key (a secret), a Domain (for example yourcompany.atlassian.net), an Email, and a Verify SSL option that allows configuring a root CA certificate.

quotes: The Jira API key field, which is a secret.
The domain of your Jira account (e.g., yourcompany.atlassian.net).
The user email of your Jira account.
Select the Verify SSL checkbox to allow the configuration of a root CA certificate to trust during the SSL negotiation in the CA certificate field.

jira-filters.statement: On the Jira Issues page, if left empty the connector retrieves all issues not filtered by a JQL condition; if a checkbox is enabled data volume might increase, and if it is not selected the connector retrieves a standard set of issue fields.

quotes: If left empty, the connector retrieves all issues not filtered by a JQL condition.
If enabled, data volume might increase. If you do not select the checkbox, the connector retrieves a standard set of issue fields.

zad-prereq.statement: The Zscaler Advanced Detections connector requires active Internet & SaaS and Agentic SOC subscriptions, and the Zscaler Account team sets it up on the customer's behalf.

quotes: To configure the Zscaler Advanced Detections connector, ensure you have active Internet & SaaS and Agentic SOC subscriptions.
Your Zscaler Account team sets up the Zscaler Advanced Detections connector on your behalf.

zad-incidents.statement: When Zscaler Advanced Detections detects a threat it publishes an incident on the Incidents page with one source labeled Zscaler Advanced Detections.

quotes: When a threat is detected, Zscaler Advanced Detections publishes an incident on the Incidents page with one source labeled Zscaler Advanced Detections.

zad-analytics.statement: Zscaler Advanced Detections uses two classes of analytics, indicators of compromise and behavioral detectors, and maps every detector to MITRE ATT&CK techniques.

quotes: using two primary classes of analytics:
- Indicators of compromise: Every piece of telemetry is tested
- Behavioral detectors: These analytics identify sequences of system activity
We map every detector to MITRE ATT&CK® techniques so you can quantify your detection coverage.

zad-threats.statement: Zscaler Advanced Detections lists unmanaged devices, insider threats, encrypted threats, "living off the land" attacks, and AI-driven and multi-stage attacks as the Zscaler-specific threats its detectors help detect earlier and stop faster.

quotes: This helps detect the following Zscaler-specific threats earlier and stop them faster:
- Unmanaged devices
- Insider threats
- Encrypted threats
- "Living off the land" attacks
- AI-driven and multi-stage attacks

okta-scope.statement: The Okta Workforce Identity connector retrieves system log activity from Okta (application, device, group, system, user authentication, user lifecycle, user MFA and zone activity) for use in the Agentic SOC application.

quotes: to retrieve crucial identity and device data for use within the Agentic SOC application
It retrieves system log activity (e.g., application, device, group, system, user authentication, user lifecycle, user multi-factor authentication (MFA), and zone activity) from Okta as telemetry

okta-auth.statement: The Okta Workforce Identity connector requires active Internet & SaaS (ZIA) and Agentic SOC accounts and offers two authentication types, Token Hostname and Okta OAuth 2.0.

quotes: ensure you have active Internet & SaaS (ZIA) and Agentic SOC accounts.
The Token Hostname authentication type requires the following parameters:
The Okta OAuth 2.0 authentication requires the following parameters:

okta-auth-window-name.statement: The Okta Workforce Identity page's authentication steps say "The Okta Users Authentication window appears."

quotes: The Okta Users Authentication window appears.

code42-scope.statement: The Code42 connector retrieves alerts from configured alert rules, including details on alert destinations and alert actors; creating the API client requires the Customer Cloud Admin role and the Alerts Read API permission, and the client ID, client secret and base URL are shown on creation.

quotes: The Code42 connector retrieves alerts from configured alert rules, including details on alert destinations and alert actors.
To create API clients, you must be assigned the Customer Cloud Admin role.
API Permissions: For Alerts, select the Read checkbox.
The generated client ID, client secret, and base URL are displayed.

code42-days.statement: On the Code42 page, the number of days to retrieve data for during each run sets the lookback period (in days) from the current date.

quotes: Enter the number of days that you want to retrieve data for during each run. This value sets the lookback period (in days) from the current date.

code42-mimecast-reference.statement: The Code42 connector page's prerequisites say "To learn more, refer to the Mimecast documentation."

quotes: To learn more, refer to the Mimecast documentation.

zia-params.statement: The ZIA Devices and Users connector retrieves devices and their owners from ZIA, and authenticates with the username and password of a ZIA admin account.

quotes: The ZIA Devices and Users connector retrieves information about devices and their owners from ZIA.
The username associated with a ZIA admin account.
The password associated with a ZIA admin account.

zia-api-key.statement: The ZIA connector needs an organization with an API subscription and an enabled API key; an organization can have only one API key, so a new one requires deleting the existing key.

quotes: ensure that your organization has an API subscription and an API key enabled.
An organization can only have one API key. If you already have an API key, creating a new API key is not possible. To create a new API key, delete the existing API key.

zia-perms.statement: For the ZIA admin who creates the API key, all permissions are set to View Only when possible, User Names and Device Information to Visible and Workflow Access to None; the user providing the username and password must be an admin with access to all functional scopes.

quotes: Configure the following permissions for the admin who creates the API key:
All permissions: When possible, set to View Only.
User Names: Set to Visible.
Device Information: Set to Visible.
Workflow Access: Set to None.
The user providing the credentials (i.e., username and password) for the configuration must be an admin with access to all functional scopes.

zia-password-login.statement: The ZIA page says that if all required parameters and appropriate permissions are entered and saving the connector still errors, the user whose credentials are entered might need Password Based Login enabled; the steps are done by logging in to the ZIA Admin Portal as a super admin and going to Administration > Administration Management.

quotes: If you entered all the required parameters with the appropriate permissions, but are still encountering an error when attempting to save the connector, you might need to enable Password Based Login for the user whose credentials you are entering into the system.
Log in to the ZIA Admin Portal as a super admin.
Go to Administration > Administration Management.

zia-cloud-company.statement: The ZIA company ID is viewed under Administration > Company Profile on the Organization tab, in the General Information section, and the cloud name is taken from the admin login URL (admin.zscalerbeta.net gives zscalerbeta.net).

quotes: Go to Administration > Company Profile.
On the Organization tab, in the General Information section, view the company ID.
if your organization logs into admin.zscalerbeta.net, then your organization's cloud name is zscalerbeta.net.

zcc-purpose.statement: The Zscaler Client Connector Devices connector retrieves data on assets in the organization, including which Zscaler products are installed on which assets.

quotes: retrieves data on assets in your organization, including which Zscaler products are installed on which assets.

zcc-prereq.statement: The ZCC connector requires the API to be enabled for the organization by contacting Zscaler Support, and an admin whose role has full access to the public API resource in the Zscaler Client Connector Portal.

quotes: you must enable the API for your organization to obtain access to the Zscaler Client Connector API by contacting Zscaler Support.
the admin must be assigned a role with full access to the public API resource in the Zscaler Client Connector Portal

zcc-api-key.statement: A ZCC API key name must be alphanumeric, cannot contain spaces and has a maximum of 50 characters; the key status defaults to Enabled, the role to select is Read access, and the recommended session validity is at least 43,200 seconds (12 hours).

quotes: The name must be alphanumeric, cannot contain spaces, and has a maximum of 50 characters.
Status: By default, Enabled is selected. If disabled, the key is unavailable to use.
Role: Select Read access for the key.
The recommended session length is at least 43,200 seconds, which is equal to 12 hours.

zcc-secret.statement: The ZCC client secret is only available when the API key is created and not after the window is closed.

quotes: Store the client secret securely because it is only available when creating an API key. It is not available after you close the window.

netbox-streams.statement: The NetBox connector has 3 streams: Devices, IP Addresses (IPAM data) and Virtual Machines.

quotes: There are three NetBox streams.
NetBox Devices: Retrieves a detailed inventory of physical and virtual network devices, including hardware types, roles, installation sites, and current operational status.
NetBox IP Addresses: Retrieves IPAM data, including networks, VRFs, VLANs, assignment status, and associations with specific devices.
NetBox Virtual Machines: Retrieves detailed virtualized infrastructure data, including virtual machine configurations, cluster associations, and resource allocations like CPU and memory.

netbox-perms.statement: The NetBox API token's user needs DCIM > Device for Devices, IPAM > IP Address for IP Addresses and Virtualization > Virtual Machine for Virtual Machines.

quotes: | NetBox Devices | DCIM > Device |
| NetBox IP Addresses | IPAM > IP Address |
| NetBox Virtual Machines | Virtualization > Virtual Machine |

netbox-token.statement: Creating a NetBox API token requires being a NetBox admin, and the token is created with Write enabled deselected; expiry and Allowed IPs are optional, and an expiring key must be refreshed to keep connectivity.

quotes: You must be a NetBox admin to create an API token.
Write enabled: Deselect the checkbox.
If an expiration date is set, make sure to refresh the key when it expires to ensure continuous connectivity.
Allowed IPs: (Optional) Enter the list of the Zscaler SecOps allowed IP addresses to restrict the use of this key to API requests originating from the specified IP addresses.

netbox-url.statement: The NetBox URL is the instance URL in the format https://<Your Instance>.cloud.netboxapp.com.

quotes: in the format https://<Your Instance>.cloud.netboxapp.com.

runzero-assets.statement: The runZero Assets stream retrieves the Get/export/org/assets.jsonl call and the Asset schema.

quotes: The runZero Assets stream retrieves the Get/export/org/assets.jsonl call and the Asset schema.

runzero-vulns.statement: The runZero Vulnerabilities stream retrieves the Get/export/org/vulnerabilities.jsonl call.

quotes: The runZero Vulnerabilities stream retrieves the Get/export/org/vulnerabilities.jsonl call.

runzero-auth.statement: The runZero Assets source authenticates with a client ID and client secret from API Clients and an organization ID, found with GET /account/orgs after authorizing with OAuth2 clientCredentials.

quotes: Click Register New API Client.
Click Authorize and enter your client ID and secret in the oauthDefaults (OAuth2, clientCredentials) section.
In the GET /account/orgs API documentation section, click Try it out.

ss-pages.statement: The SecurityScorecard Alerts source has a Username field for the user that receives the relevant notifications.

quotes: In the field, enter the username that receives the relevant notifications.

ss-fields.statement: The SecurityScorecard source has Identifier and Category retrieval fields.

quotes: - Identifier
- Category

sftp.statement: The SFTP stream retrieves files from any remote server that supports SFTP, using a username, password and host (hostname or IP address).

quotes: The SFTP stream allows you to retrieve your files from any remote server that supports SFTP.
The hostname or IP address associated with the host server.
A valid username associated with the host server.
A valid password associated with the user account on the host server.

sftp-filters.statement: The SFTP source selects CSV or JSON files, takes an optional folder path (all relevant files if empty, so reports/2023 excludes reports/2024), a start date in YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00Z format and a regex files pattern.

quotes: From the drop-down menu, select CSV or JSON format.
If left empty, all relevant files are retrieved.
Enter a start date for the data retrieval in the YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00Z format.
Enter the files that the connector filters to monitor or ingest data.
In the field, enter the path to the specific folder you want to retrieve.
For example, entering reports/2023 only retrieves files from that specific folder. Files from the reports/2024 or personnel folders are not retrieved.
Files Pattern (Regex)

limited-availability-meaning.title: What limited availability restricts on the connector pages that mark it
limited-availability-meaning.detail: Among the connector pages, the pages cited in limited-availability, the Horizon3.ai Weaknesses Evidence stream and others (Microsoft Entra ID, the Rapid7 InsightVM Policy Compliance stream, SentinelOne streams, the Veracode Applications stream) mark limited availability and say to contact Zscaler Support; none of the connector pages read says what limited availability restricts, who is eligible or whether the connector is supported.

sync-behaviour.title: Run frequency, incremental versus full pulls and the handling of records outside a lookback window on the connector pages
sync-behaviour.detail: The connector pages in the captures give per-run lookback fields (for example Aqua Security, Axonius, Bitsight, Code42) or a Start Date, but the connector configuration pages read do not state the run frequency, the cursor, or what happens to records outside the window. The uvm-configuring-discovery-settings page gives a Scan Frequency, which is not a statement for these connectors.

stream-field-mappings.title: Which UVM fields each connector stream populates
stream-field-mappings.detail: The connector pages read do not describe the field mappings or asset and finding schemas each stream populates; several pages refer to a Zscaler and vendor Deployment Guide that is not captured.
